              COMPLAINT AND REQUEST FOR FAST TRACK PROCESSING

       Pursuant to sections 202(c), 306 and 309 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”)1 and Rule 206

of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or “Commission”) Rules of Practice and

Procedure,2 Northern Indiana Public Service Company LLC (“NIPSCO”) submits this Complaint

and request for fast track processing against Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc.

(“MISO”) to establish a rate schedule under the MISO Open Access Transmission, Energy and

Operating Reserve Markets Tariff (“OATT” or “Tariff”) that would provide a mechanism for

NIPSCO to recover all costs associated with NIPSCO’s compliance with a recent order from the

U.S. Secretary of Energy.3

       On December 23, 2025, the U.S. Secretary of Energy issued an order pursuant to section

202(c) of the FPA and section 301(b) of the Department of Energy Organization Act4 determining

that “an emergency exists in portions of the Midwest region of the United States due to a shortage

I.     EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

       Section 202(c) of the FPA vests the Secretary of Energy with authority to determine when

an emergency exists due to shortages of electric energy, generation, or related facilities, and to

order such temporary generation and dispatch as is necessary to meet that emergency and serve

the public interest. Under the statutory framework established by the Department of Energy

Organization Act, the Commission’s role in this process is limited but critical: ensuring just and

reasonable compensation for entities compelled to provide this emergency service.

       On December 23, 2025, the Secretary of Energy exercised the authority under section

202(c) and issued an order directing MISO and NIPSCO to take all measures necessary to ensure

the continued availability and operation of the Impacted Schahfer Units.         Specifically, the

Secretary of Energy determined that “an emergency exists by reason of a sudden increase in the

demand for electric energy, or a shortage of electric energy or of facilities for the generation or

transmission of electric energy” in the MISO region, and that continued operation of the Impacted

Schahfer Units will best meet the emergency and serve the public interest.11

        The DOE 202(c) Order confirms that rate recovery is available pursuant to section 202(c)

and directs NIPSCO to file with the Commission any tariff revisions or waivers necessary to

effectuate the Order.12 After consultation with MISO, NIPSCO determined, similar to Consumers

Energy, that filing a Complaint with the Commission is the only available procedural mechanism

to add a schedule to the MISO Tariff to allow rate recovery pursuant to the DOE 202(c) Order. 13

Importantly, as part of this Complaint, NIPSCO is not seeking a determination of any specific

costs to be recovered. Rather, following the model of the Consumers Energy proceeding, NIPSCO

is seeking to establish a rate schedule in the MISO Tariff and will subsequently make a separate

filing to present actual, just and reasonable costs incurred to comply with the DOE 202(c) Order,

net of market revenues.14

       As described herein, the MISO Tariff currently lacks a provision to address cost recovery

for NIPSCO in response to the DOE 202(c) Order nor does it contain a basis for allocating such

costs in a manner consistent with the nature and scope of a federally-declared emergency. Absent

Commission action, NIPSCO’s statutory right to recover its costs associated with the DOE 202(c)

Order would be rendered illusory. The Commission has clear authority to address this concern.

Sections 202(c), 306 and 309 of the FPA empower the Commission to prescribe just and reasonable

compensation for emergency service and to take all actions necessary to carry out that

responsibility. Given that cost recovery under section 202(c) operates independently of the

traditional ratemaking strictures of sections 205 and 206 of the FPA and expressly contemplates

 III.   BACKGROUND

       A.      Parties

               1.        Northern Indiana Public Service Company LLC

       NIPSCO is an Indiana limited liability company headquartered in Merrillville, Indiana and

is a subsidiary of NiSource Inc. NIPSCO serves approximately 871,000 natural gas customers and

492,700 electric customers, or 1.3 million total customers across Northern Indiana. NIPSCO owns

and operates approximately 3,880 megawatts of electric generating capacity and 2,981 miles of

electric transmission lines. NIPSCO is an electric load-serving entity and a transmission-owning

member of MISO. NIPSCO has transferred functional control of its transmission system to MISO,

which serves as NIPSCO’s Reliability Coordinator.

               2.        Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc.

       MISO is an Independent System Operator and Regional Transmission Organization and is

authorized by the Commission to provide open access transmission service and to administer

wholesale energy, capacity, and ancillary services markets in portions of the Midwest region of

the United States, as well as certain other regions. MISO also administers the MISO Tariff, which

governs such markets. MISO includes ten separate pricing zones. MISO’s northern and central

regions contain zones 1 through 7.

 V.     ARGUMENT

       A.        NIPSCO Has a Right to Recover Costs Associated with the DOE 202(c)
                 Order, Which Can Be Determined After-the-Fact

       FPA section 202(c) provides a right to recover costs incurred in complying with an

emergency order (“Order Costs”). When the affected parties cannot agree on such costs, the statute

assigns FERC the responsibility to determine them. FERC may resolve cost recovery issues under

section 202(c) and may do so even after a section 202(c) order expires and after the conclusion of

the mandatory provision of generation and/or jurisdictional service.

                 1.      Parties Subject to a Section 202(c) Order are Entitled to Recover
                         Associated Costs, Subject to FERC Approval

       There is no reasonable dispute that NIPSCO has a statutory right to recover all of its Order

Costs, net of market revenues. This entitlement is established by the plain language of FPA section

202(c), the DOE Referral Regulation, and the DOE 202(c) Order, itself:

       •     FPA section 202(c): If the parties affected by such order fail to agree upon the terms
             of any arrangement between them in carrying out such order, the Commission, after
             hearing held either before or after such order takes effect, may prescribe by
             supplemental order such terms as it finds to be just and reasonable, including the
             compensation or reimbursement which should be paid to or by any such party.34

       •     DOE Referral Regulation: In the event that the DOE determines that an emergency
             exists under [FPA] section 202(c), and the “entities” are unable to agree on the rates to
             be charged, the DOE shall prescribe the conditions of service and refer the rate issues
             to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission for determination by that agency in
             accordance with its standards and procedures.35

       •     DOE 202(c) Order: “Rate recovery is available pursuant to 16 U.S.C. § 824a(c).”36

       Indeed, recovery of Order Costs is also mandated by the U.S. Constitution. Specifically,

the Fifth Amendment Takings Clause bars the federal government from taking private property

                   2.      Pursuant to the Commission’s Section 202(c) Rate Authority, Costs

                           Emergency Generation or Provision of Jurisdictional Service Without

         As discussed below, both the plain text of section 202(c) and prior Commission precedent

confirm that appropriate compensation can be determined and recovered after the effective date of

an order declaring an emergency and/or requiring provision of jurisdictional service and costs have

begun to be incurred. Moreover, the prior notice requirements and related filed rate doctrine and

rule against retroactive ratemaking pursuant to FPA sections 205 and 206 do not apply in the

context of determining compensation pursuant to FPA section 202(c), which provides independent

ratemaking authority and includes its own “just and reasonable” standard.

         First, pursuant to section 202(c)’s plain text, after an emergency section 202(c) order “takes

On December 23, 2025, the U.S. Secretary of Energy (“Secretary”) issued an order pursuant to
section 202(c) of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”), 16 U.S.C. § 824a(c), and section 301(b) of the
Department of Energy Organization Act, 42 U.S.C. § 7151(b), determining that an emergency
exists in portions of the Midwest region of the United States due to a shortage of electric energy,
a shortage of facilities for the generation of electric energy, and other causes. See Department of
Energy, Order No. 202-25-12 (“DOE Order”). The DOE Order compelled Midcontinent
Independent System Operator, Inc. (“MISO”) and Northern Indiana Public Service Company LLC
(“NIPSCO”) to ensure the continued operation and availability of NIPSCO’s R.M. Schahfer
Generating Station Units 17 and 18 (“Schahfer Units 17 and 18”) from December 23, 2025,
through March 23, 2025, as such time may be extended by subsequent order of the Secretary (the
“Order Duration Period”).

       The Secretary ordered MISO and NIPSCO to take all measures necessary to ensure that
the Schahfer Plant is available to operate during the Order Duration Period. The DOE Order also
orders MISO to “take every step to employ economic dispatch of Schahfer Units 17 and 18 to
minimize cost to ratepayers.” The DOE Order confirms that rate recovery is available pursuant to
FPA section 202(c).

       Costs associated with the DOE Order have been incurred, and will continue to be incurred,
before and during the Order Duration Period (“Order Costs”). NIPSCO shall petition FERC to
approve recovery of Order Costs, net of market revenues, that FERC determines are recoverable
pursuant to section 202(c) (“Recoverable Order Costs”).

       This Schedule 56 shall allocate the Recoverable Order Costs incurred to comply with the
DOE Order, and any extensions of the same or subsequent orders by the Secretary, in the following
manner. MISO shall allocate the Recoverable Order Costs to load-serving entities (“LSEs”) in the
Zones 1-7 (or such successor zone designations reflecting the Northern and Central MISO Zones)
(“Affected LSEs”) on a load ratio share basis. For purposes of the calculation described in this
Schedule 56, the load ratio share shall be the factor calculated as the Actual Energy Withdrawals
plus Export Schedules of a Market Participant at all Commercial Pricing Nodes, other than
Coordinated Transaction Schedules and Export Schedules for External Asynchronous Resources,
divided by the sum of all the Actual Energy Withdrawals plus Export Schedules at all Commercial
Pricing Nodes, other than Coordinated Transaction Schedules and Export Schedules for External
Asynchronous Resources, in Zones 1-7 (i.e., the Northern and Central MISO Zones).

LSE load ratio share (AFF_LSE_SHARE) by the Recoverable Order Costs (REC_
